items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — went straight from the callback greeting into recapping the quote form
Never asked the customer's name or how she was doing; she volunteered 'this is Margaret' and Joel never used it once in 9 minutes
Never proactively confirmed availability for Friday the 28th — the customer had to ask 'what time could you start on Friday?' at the very end
No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) never mentioned; 'insurance' was listed as included with no explanation and no 60c/lb baseline
'No hidden fees' pitch only partial — said 'no additional fees tacked on last minute' but never itemized no credit card fees / no fuel surcharge / no transportation fees / no assembly fees
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing — no prep-lowers-the-bill framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, on a call where the customer explicitly balked at the hours
Crew size only given because the customer asked ('how many movers?'); truck count never stated
No equivalents or concrete reference points to justify the 4-6 hour range when the customer pushed back that her past moves 'take but two hours'
No booking attempt — customer said 'let me get back to you' and Joel accepted it with no ask for the business
Confirmation email not explained — only 'I'll send over a quote here'; no bolded-details list, no 'reply with any corrections', no hours or how to reach us
Garbled price delivery: '$1,070 or sorry, $1,000 $90,090' and start time read as '83845' — the two numbers that mattered most on this call were the least clear
No COI / building-requirement question despite both ends being elevator buildings (storage facility and condo)
top_strength: Discovery and the clock explanation were genuinely strong — Joel confirmed the full move profile off the quote form, asked walk distance at BOTH ends, probed heavy/fragile items, appliances, box count, and surfaced a second storage unit the customer hadn't mentioned. His clock section was complete and clean: on-site start, contract signing, walkthrough, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, and a sense-check.
coaching_note: When Margaret said 'I totally did not expect to be paying this kind... taking this much time,' that was the moment the call was won or lost — and Joel answered it with a defense of the estimate instead of a plan. That is exactly what Save Your Ass is for: 'Here's how you shrink that bill — consolidate the loose items, bag the small stuff, take a carload of the delicate things yourself, and every one of those saves you 15-minute increments.' It reframes him as her advocate on price instead of the guy quoting six hours. Pair it with an equivalent she can picture ('a full 10x10 is about a school bus worth of volume, and every trip goes through two elevators') so the number stops feeling arbitrary. He also never asked for the booking after she asked about Friday start times — that was a buying signal, and the call ended on 'let me get back to you' with no deposit-free, no-risk close offered.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient with light affirmations ('Awesome,' 'Cool,' 'sounds good'), but entirely transactional — zero use of Margaret's name, no empathy when she voiced sticker shock, and she ended the call non-committal.
